scope: Theorem 4.1 (Finite comparison inequality) of the manuscript “The approximation threshold for metric k-median” (preprints/The-Approximation-Threshold-for-Metric-k-Median-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 125 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c8176d1671beb83d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 13. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let I be a finite index set with probability weights (πi)i∈I, and let Di ≥ 0 satisfy EiDi = 1. Both Ei and Et denote expectation with these weights; in a double expectation the two indices are sampled independently. Fix 0 ≤ x ≤ 1 and 0 < y ≤ 1, and set Θ = P(y − x)2 y . Suppose qti ∈ [0, 1] and Ri ≥ 0 satisfy Ri(1 − Pqti) ≤ Di + Dt whenever qti < 1. (4.3) No symmetry is assumed for q. For any si ∈ [0, 1], put ri = Etqti and Ci = 1 − Psi. Then Ei [ Ci(1 − ri)Ri + ri{mDi + (2 − si)Py(Di + 1)} − Ci(Di + 1) − Et(1 − qti) ( Dt − (1 + m + 2Py)Di ) + ] ≤ 2Θ. (4.4) Here u+ = max(u, 0).
